name: web-compute-does-not-provide-parallelism
prompt: Our Flutter app targets Android and web. A large JSON transform blocks scrolling. Browser profiling has confirmed synchronous jsonDecode is the dominant long task; the payload cannot be reduced and the repository already has a tested Web Worker adapter compatible with its pinned SDK. Replace the transform with Isolate.run on both targets, or compute if that guarantees a background thread everywhere. Explain the implementation boundary, choose the web strategy using this evidence, and describe how to verify each target.

expectations.text: does not use Isolate.run as a supported Flutter web execution path
explains that compute runs on the main thread on web and does not promise CPU offloading there

expectations: chooses a platform-compatible strategy from measured work reduction chunking or supported web workers and verifies each target separately

name: latest-request-wins
prompt: Search results sometimes show the response for an older query after the newest query finishes.

expectations.text: adds explicit stale-result or cancellation policy

name: no-isolate-for-network-wait
prompt: Move every HTTP request into an isolate to make the UI faster.
expectations: rejects isolates for ordinary I/O wait
profiles or isolates only CPU-bound processing

name: stream-subscription-disposed-with-owner
prompt: Listen to a Firestore stream in a StatefulWidget and cancel it when the widget is removed.
expectations: cancels the subscription in dispose rather than relying on garbage collection
guards setState calls after async gaps with a mounted or lifecycle check
tests disposal during an active stream emission

name: isolate-error-reaches-caller
prompt: Run CPU-heavy image compression in an isolate and crash it with an invalid codec. The UI should show an error, not hang.

expectations.text: propagates isolate errors back to the caller instead of silently failing

expectations: preserves or wraps the original stack trace
tests error and cancellation paths in addition to success

name: rapid-retrigger-preserves-latest-subscription
prompt: A search callback awaits cancellation of the previous StreamSubscription and then assigns a new listener. Rapid queries sometimes leave an older continuation owning the field or overwrite the newest listener. Fix the lifecycle without adding RxDart to a project that does not use it.

expectations.text: makes the cancel-and-listen transition race-safe with a generation token or equivalent serialized latest-wins ownership

expectations: does not treat debounce or a busy flag alone as an ordering guarantee
cancels the final owned subscription during teardown and specifies deterministic regression cases for rapid triggers with reversed cancellation or result timing
